text:
Alex: FYI noticed a regression on new tenant onboard where CP endpoint attach latency spikes and sometimes fails. looks like ENI create throttles in us-east-1 during heavy onboards. filing this thread to capture short-term mitigations + long-term tradeoffs between peering vs Privatelink-like endpoints.

Priya: oh bad. is this the same attach lambda that creates ENIs on relay hosts? any recent deploys?

Alex: yes, the attach lambda. no deploys at the exact time. cloudtrail shows CreateNetworkInterface throttling + ThrottlingException. also a few complaints from k8s nodes hitting instance ENI limits.

Devon: two orthogonal problems: 1) ENI API rate limits (CreateNetworkInterface) and 2) instance-level NIC limits (eni-per-instance). our current playbook creates ENI on demand per-tenant. options: pre-warm ENI pools, move to cross-account Privatelink endpoints, or switch to regional peering + relays. tradeoffs: pre-warm = fast attach but eats IPs; Privatelink = fewer per-tenant IPs but more VPC endpoint service mgmt and SNAT complexity; peering = simpler L3 but requires route propagation and cross-account peering scale.

Helena: can we do per-az pre-warm with TTL and reclaim? like keep N ENIs per AZ per account tagged cp:warm. then attach just does AttachNetworkInterface by id which is cheaper? AWS still charges and uses IPs but avoids CreateNetworkInterface spikes.

Priya: attach-by-id still needs AttachNetworkInterface call. but avoiding create reduces API ops. also need reclaim policy so we don't run out of IPs in small subnets. a reclaimer that runs GC after idle TTL and emits metric cp.warm_eni_utilization could work.

Alex: what about using ENI trunking on larger instance types to increase per-instance ENI capacity? that reduces instance-limit failures but changes instance fleet/cost.

Devon: yes trunking helps but not always available across cloud partners and it raises ops complexity (different AMIs, enhanced networking). also some customers won't allow large instances in their VPC.

Helena: Privatelink option: publish a VPC Endpoint Service in our CP VPC and customers create an interface endpoint to that service in their VPC. Pros: no cross-account peering, interface endpoints are per-AZ and managed by AWS. Cons: customers must create endpoints (self-serve friction), data path might go over AWS-managed network with different egress semantics and costs, and we need to handle per-tenant auth at the NLB layer.

Priya: plus interface endpoints use ENIs under the hood but are created in the customer account per endpoint. that pushes ENI burden to customer side, which may or may not be desirable. also Privatelink supports a per-account endpoint quota. not a silver bullet.

Devon: regional relay/peering model: create a regional relay VPC we peer into customer VPCs (or route via transit). Pros: simpler routing, can aggregate many tenants on relay instances. Cons: peering scale (lots of peering attachments), cross-account route limits, and potential for single relay to become blast radius.

Alex: experimentally, I prefer hybrid: try ENI pre-warm + concurrency limiter first to stop spikes. in parallel spike a small test of Privatelink for a handful of customers who opt in. get metrics for API rates and endpoint latencies.

infra-bot: alert: cp.attach.createNetworkInterface ThrottlingException rate > 5/min in us-east-1 between 2025-01-12T14:03 and 14:05. Created ticket INFRA-CP-ENI-987.

Priya: implementation checklist for pre-warm: 
- agent warm-pool manager: create N ENIs per subnet with tag cp:pool=warm account=<acct> az=<az>
- TTL: 15m idle, GC at 5m intervals, soft-limit per-subnet with accounting metric
- attach workflow buys an ENI id from pool (atomic lease) and does AttachNetworkInterface; if none, fallback to create with backoff
- expose metrics: warm_pool_size, warm_pool_free, attach_by_path(create|lease), attach_errors_by_code

Devon: add spike protection: global in-region limiter for create calls, and per-host attach concurrency cap so we don't create >M ENIs concurrently from one instance. implement a leaky-bucket.

Helena: runbook edits: if attach ThrottlingException: 
- check warm_pool_free metric and recent GC runs
- if warm_pool_free > 0 but attach failing, check AccessDenied/AssumeRole errors
- temporary mitigation: enable relay-fallback flag for customer (routes to regional relay) and notify customer status as degraded

Alex: for Privatelink trial we need a small onboarding doc: steps for customers to create interface endpoint and accept service endpoint. also note cost and endpoint quota constraints. Priya can own that doc?

Priya: yes I'll draft it. also will add an automation preflight: validate subnet IP availability and ENI quotas via DescribeAccountAttributes + DescribeNetworkInterfaces counts before onboarding.

Devon: timeline: prototype warm-pool + limiter in one sprint, canary to 10% of onboards. Privatelink trial as parallel spike with 2 customers. keep peering as last-resort because of scale.

Helena: +1. please add a dashboard panel for "attach_path" breakdown and a table with per-account ENI consumption so support can triage quickly.

Alex: assigning owners: Priya -> warm-pool GC + preflight doc; Devon -> concurrency limiter + metrics; Helena -> fallback routing + dashboard. will recheck next Wed.

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-CP-ENI-987 updated: subtasks created (warm-pool, limiter, privatelink-trial).
